1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Describe the sources of excessive emissions: location, type of industry, and description of the emission parameters (e.g., [extract_itex]PM_{2.5}[/extract_itex], [extract_itex]PM_{10}[/extract_itex], [extract_itex]SO_{2}[/extract_itex], [extract_itex]NO_{x}[/extract_itex], [extract_itex]VOCs[/extract_itex], etc.).
3. Check available data on emission standards and limits.
4. Analyze trends in emissions over time.
5. Consider factors affecting emissions (e.g., weather, production schedule).
6. Describe any trends in the emission data.
7. Calculate the total amount of pollutants emitted.
8. Assess the risk to human health and the environment.
9. Recommend actions to reduce excessive emissions.
10. Include maps and charts showing the distribution
